title: Revisiting Graph Autoencoders as Implicit Contrastive Learners

problem.claim: Graph autoencoders and graph contrastive learning are often studied in isolation as fundamentally different approaches.

gap.claim: Contrastive view design, especially asymmetric views caused by mismatched subgraph views, is underexplored in graph autoencoder research.

contributions.claim: The work conceptualizes structure-based and feature-based graph autoencoders as implicit graph contrastive learners.
The work introduces a unified formulation that places contrastive view design at the center of graph autoencoder analysis.
The work formalizes the framework and examines its impact on performance and efficiency through systematic experiments on representative graph learning tasks.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that interpreting graph autoencoders as implicit contrastive learners provides a clearer understanding of existing models.
The authors report that their perspective provides practical guidance for designing effective and scalable graph autoencoders.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph autoencoders and graph contrastive learning are presented as major but separated paradigms.
The work reframes graph autoencoders as implicit graph contrastive learners and attributes their differences mainly to contrastive view construction.
A unified formulation emphasizes contrastive view design and asymmetric views as an underexplored axis.
Systematic experiments examine the impact of the framework on performance and efficiency.
The authors report improved conceptual understanding and practical guidance for effective, scalable graph autoencoder design.

source_observation.claim: Graph autoencoders can be analyzed as implicit contrastive learners whose differences may lie primarily in contrastive view construction.

interpretation.claim: When comparing self-supervised graph models, inspect view construction separately from objectives and architectures.

application.claim: Use contrastive view design, including possible asymmetry, as an explicit dimension when designing or analyzing graph autoencoders.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that view construction is the primary differentiator for all graph autoencoder variants or tasks.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the unified formulation's mathematical details.
The abstract does not identify the representative tasks, datasets, baselines, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not report the conditions under which asymmetric views improve performance or efficiency.
